{"id":"mimid-604m.7","title":"Agent::in_transaction commits twice for every transaction","description":"Agent::in_transaction opens with self.save() before BEGIN IMMEDIATE:

    // What was delivered before is saved on its own first.
    self.save()?;

crate::state::save UPDATEs the agent_state row unconditionally, so that
pre-save always dirties a page and, with nothing else holding a
transaction, is a committed write transaction of its own. Every
in_transaction call therefore costs two commits, not one, and
in_transaction is how the agent builds every Commit, handles every
server Message and ends every outbox entry.

Measured on the first-private-message path, after bead mimid-604m.6
batched Agent::host_room: host_room commits 4 times, of which 2 are the
one transaction and its pre-save, 1 is the save after Room/create and 1
is publishing this device's first KeyPackage.

## Why it is not just removable

The pre-save is what makes a rollback safe to be coarse. Agent::roll_back
reads the state back from the database and reloads the groups, discarding
whatever the in-memory state held; the pre-save is what puts the
already-delivered journal entries, and any state change made before the
call, where the rollback can find them. Skipping it when
self.undelivered is empty would still drop in-memory state changes made
before the call, and the set of callers that have one is not obvious from
the call sites.

So this is a durability question about what a rollback is allowed to
lose, not a refactor: for Mark. If the answer is that in_transaction may
keep the pre-save only when there is something to save, every agent write
costs one commit instead of two.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-28T02:08:28.286639076Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-28T02:08:28.286639076Z","labels":["human"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-604m.7","depends_on_id":"mimid-604m","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-28T02:08:28.324596796Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"MEASURED, 2026-11-27. The pre-save writes nothing new on 712 of 717
calls. Instrumentation added, run, and removed; nothing committed.

THE SHAPE IS REAL, and now shown rather than read. Agent::in_transaction
(crates/mimid-agent-core/src/agent.rs) calls self.save() before
BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and crate::state::save issues
"UPDATE agent_state SET record = ?1 WHERE user = ?2" with no condition,
inside SAVEPOINT agent_save. A probe around that pre-save reported, on
every one of the 18 calls of a two-provider message run:

  autocommit=true        before it: nothing else holds a transaction, so
                         the pre-save is a transaction of its own
  rows=1                 the UPDATE reported a row changed, although the
                         serialised record was byte-identical to the
                         stored one
  still_autocommit=true  after it: that transaction closed, i.e. it
                         committed, before BEGIN IMMEDIATE

Nothing sets PRAGMA synchronous, so SQLite's default FULL stands and in
WAL mode each of those commits fsyncs the WAL.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND WHY IT IS SOUND. A probe before the pre-save
serialised self.state with the same serde_json call state::save uses and
compared it to the stored agent_state row, and reported
self.undelivered.is_empty() beside it. Those two are the whole of what
state::save writes -- the record and the journal append -- so when the
record matches and the journal is empty the pre-save's entire effect is
an UPDATE of identical bytes. Not a dirty flag: a flag would have to be
set by every writer of self.state and would measure the instrumentation's
own completeness rather than the state.

The probe can report a difference. The same comparison placed at the
post-step save inside in_transaction reported differs=true and
journal=true on the Commit and send paths in the same runs, so
differs=false before the pre-save is a result and not a dead probe.

THE COUNTS. Two providers, a daemon and a JMAP client each,
sync_interval_ms = 3600000 so no poll can account for anything, phase
markers between actions. Call sites named by #[track_caller].

  action                 in_transaction  dirty  clean
  first private message        10          0     10
  second in that room           4          0      4
  a message the other way       4          0      4

The first-message phase is the direct Chat (room build, Commit, Welcome),
the send, and the arrival: 7 at the sender's, 3 at the receiver's, call
sites host_room, build_commit, send_update, receive, join,
send_content_with (twice). Steady state is 4 either way: three at the
sender (send_content_with twice, then receive for her own echo) and one
at the receiver (receive). So an ordinary message costs 8 commits across
the two agents where 4 would do.

The IRC path of this bead's parent, private_queries_are_one_to_one_rooms
(crates/mimid-agent/tests/irc_v2.rs): 22 calls, 0 dirty.

THE WHOLE SUITE, which is where the one exception is. cargo test
-p mimid-agent-core --all-features: 717 pre-saves, 5 dirty. All 5 differ
in one field, pinned_scids, and all 5 are at build_commit. The writer is
Agent::invite's KeyMaterial/fetch loop (agent.rs around line 1869):

    self.state.pinned_scids = pins;
    target = identity.to_owned();
    ...
    self.commit(room, &adds, &[], &[update], "invite").await

It sets the contact's pinned SCID in memory with no save of its own and
relies on the next in_transaction's pre-save to put it on disk. That is
the only caller in the suite that does.

WHAT roll_back RESTORES. Quoted:

    fn roll_back(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.connection().execute_batch("ROLLBACK");
        self.undelivered.clear();
        self.deferred_leaver = None;
        match crate::state::read(self.connection(), &self.me) {
            Ok(state) => self.state = state,
            Err(why) => tracing::error!(
                name: "agent_state_not_reread",
                reason = why,
                "after a rollback the agent state could not be read again"
            ),
        }
        self.load_members();
    }

Four things: the open transaction goes, undelivered journal entries are
dropped, deferred_leaver is cleared, and self.state is replaced by what
state::read finds in the agent_state row. load_members then rebuilds
self.members from that state via Member::load, so the groups come from
the rolled-back OpenMLS tables.

So the recovery point is exactly the agent_state row. The pre-save's job
is to make that row equal the in-memory state at the moment of entry.

WHAT A CONDITIONAL PRE-SAVE WOULD LOSE: nothing, by construction. When
the serialised record already equals the row and undelivered is empty,
the row already is the in-memory state, so the recovery point after
skipping the write is the same row with the same bytes. The guard has to
be both halves, because roll_back clears undelivered: entries that are
durable before the attempt must not become entries that are dropped by
it. And Agent::invite's pin is not an argument against the condition but
an instance of it -- pinned_scids differs there, so a conditional
pre-save still runs and still commits the pin. The case the condition
does not cover is removing the pre-save outright, which would lose a
contact's SCID pin on a failed invite Commit.

WHAT THE CHOICE COSTS EITHER WAY. Keeping it: one extra WAL commit and
one fsync on every Commit, every received Message and every outbox
entry, writing bytes that are already there 99.3% of the time, and 8
commits instead of 4 for an ordinary message across two agents. Making
it conditional: one SELECT of the agent_state row per in_transaction,
no fsync, on the page the UPDATE would have dirtied anyway, and the
durability promise is unchanged because the condition is the statement
that the write is a no-op. The residual risk is not in roll_back but in
callers like Agent::invite that mutate state and let the next
in_transaction persist it: they keep working, but they become callers
whose correctness rests on the condition being right rather than on the
write being unconditional.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no conditional pre-save, no removal, no fix
bead. The instrumentation was a temporary probe in state.rs and agent.rs
and a temporary test, all three removed; the worktree is clean at
0167c011 and nothing was committed."}
